angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 500,904 km at 78.89 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.6763 +/- 0.0102 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 78.89 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.72 +/- 0.029 solar radii from Stalport et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1453 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...696A..86S/abstract): 500,904 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.715 +/- 0.035 solar masses from Stalport et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1453 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...696A..86S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4975 +/- 68 K from Stalport et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1453 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...696A..86S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stalport et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1453 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...696A..86S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1453.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.578, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
